slice: full-coverage-recapture: the pins two closed receipts still name

landed_against.rule: R-17 -- this receipt moves no baseline. It declares readings the campaign's own re-capture (641695d) already landed, for the two closed receipts whose recorded values the re-capture moved.

what_landed: Two closed receipts pin values the full-coverage re-capture moved again: the fingerprints ledger's correction records the exact baseline's three moved per-attacker totals, and the two P4D classifications record the identities and the ordinal they measured on their own tree. Neither is edited. Each reading is declared here instead, naming the claim it supersedes, and the assertions that read them resolve through the same chain the Phase 4 boundary's owed population does.
why_each_moved: Two causes. Lulu's Whimsy served a rank-1 cooldown at every rank, so the roster fight fits another cast and the exact baseline's two affected totals rise by it. And the pair walk's preview arming grew from two rows to twenty-seven when the certified multi-part row began publishing one event per part, which renumbers every per-pair event identity after it -- the records themselves are field-for-field unmoved.
how_to_reproduce: python scripts/golden_snapshot.py capture-coupled --exact scripts/golden_coupled_exact.json for the two totals; for the identities, read coupled_scenarios/cleaver_bloodsong_roster/combat/events out of scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json and pair its members by event_id.

supersedes.why: Lulu's Whimsy served a cooldown frozen at rank 1 (ten seconds where the cache falls to eight by rank three), so the roster fight now fits another cast. Her outgoing total carries that cast and the enemy it lands on carries the same 1.7. The fingerprints correction recorded the values the boundary re-capture left; this campaign moved them again, and this row is that claim.
